Mount
MOUNT
n.
Webster 1828 treats MOUNT as noun from Latin mons, a heap or elevation: a mass of earth or rock rising above the surrounding land, used in Scripture both of Sinai and of small hillocks of witness (Genesis 31). Also a mound or bulwark (Jeremiah 6:6). As verb: to rise, to ascend, to get upon an elevated place. This page fills the KJV-gap common of the height where God meets man. Companion pages already treat sinai, zion, and covenant.

Biblical Definition

Mount in Scripture is not a scenic overlook and not a self-made high place. It is the elevation God names, comes down upon, and forbids men to climb in their own fire. The LORD came down upon mount Sinai and called Moses up (Exo 19:20). Trust is not a mood: they that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed (Psa 125:1). The new covenant will not send you back to the mount that might be touched and that burned with fire (Heb 12:18). You are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God (Heb 12:22). Moses abode in the mount forty days to receive the tables of the covenant (Deu 9:9). The dictionary therefore keeps mount from becoming either tourism or a throne of the heart. It is the Bible’s way of saying: God descends, or you do not arrive.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines MOUNT as noun: a mass of earth or rock rising above the surrounding land; a mound or bulwark; formerly a bank of money. Verb intransitive: to rise on high; to ascend; to tower; to get on horseback. Verb transitive: to raise aloft; to climb; to furnish with horses; to carry guns. He cites Genesis 31, Jeremiah 6:6, Job 39:27, and Jeremiah 51:53.

expand to see more

MOUNT, noun [Latin mons, literally a heap or an elevation.]

1. A mass of earth, or earth and rock, rising considerably above the common surface of the surrounding land. mount is used for an eminence or elevation of earth, indefinite in highth or size, and may be a hillock, hill or mountain. We apply it to mount Blanc, in Switzerland, to mount Tom and mount Holyoke, in Massachusetts, and it is applied in Scripture to the small hillocks on which sacrifice was offered as well as to mount Sinai. Jacob offered sacrifice on the mount or heap of stones raised for a witness between him and Laban. Genesis 31:21.

2. A mound; a bulwark for offense or defense.

Hew ye down trees and cast a mount against Jerusalem. Jeremiah 6:6.

MOUNT, verb intransitive

1. To rise on high; to ascend; with or without up.

Doth the eagle mount up at thy command? Job 39:27.

2. To rise; to ascend; to tower; to be built to a great altitude.

Though Babylon should mount up to heaven. Jeremiah 51:53.

MOUNT, verb transitive To raise aloft; to lift on high.

1. To ascend; to climb; to get upon an elevated place; as, to mount a throne.

Key Scripture

Exo 19:20 — "And the LORD came down upon mount Sinai, on the top of the mount: and the LORD called Moses up to the top of the mount; and Moses went up."

Psa 125:1 — "A Song of degrees. They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever."

Heb 12:18 — "For ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest,"

Heb 12:22 — "But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels,"

Deu 9:9 — "When I was gone up into the mount to receive the tables of stone, even the tables of the covenant which the LORD made with you, then I abode in the mount forty days and forty nights, I neither did eat bread nor drink water:"

Modern Corruption

Mount is corrupted when Sinai is recast as a wellness retreat, when Zion is sold as a political brand, and when men mount their own thrones and call the climb piety.

expand to see more

The first corruption is Sinai as scenery. Exodus 19:20 is the LORD coming down, not a hike with a view. The age keeps the mountain and drops the fire. Tourism is not covenant.

The second corruption is Zion as a slogan. Psalm 125:1 trusts in the LORD and is as mount Zion. The recovery is not a flag. Hebrews 12:22 is come unto mount Sion, the city of the living God — not a campaign stop.

The third corruption is the heart that mounts. Isaiah 14:13 would sit upon the mount of the congregation. Hebrews 12:18 says ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched. Self-exaltation is not ascent.

Usage

"Sinai: the LORD came down upon mount Sinai (Exo 19:20); Moses abode in the mount forty days (Deu 9:9)."

"Trust: they that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion (Psa 125:1)."

"Covenant: not the mount that might be touched (Heb 12:18), but mount Sion and the city of the living God (Heb 12:22)."
